item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The item is neat, and completely in character for MC&D*, and I like it just for its primary property.

*(Except perhaps the part where the targets report fake memories to explain their injuries- what good is a punishment that convinces the subject that they haven't been punished? It would work better if they understood what the shooter had done to them, but could only discuss it privately with the person who pulled the trigger, and cited the false memories in any other context… but then, maybe it does work that way, and a private conversation between shooter and target is an experimental condition the Foundation hasn't tested.)

Still, the best part of the article is the last addendum. I know this isn't their thought process, but I can't help thinking "The Foundation has no problem with repeatedly using what is obviously a very effective and deliberate implement of torture, for the sole purpose of understanding what it does and how… but when they find out it also heals people, they need to change their procedures right away."

(I imagine that if you fired it at yourself, you might get both the shooter and the target effects in one go- you'd lose memories of one trauma, and gain memories of a new one to replace it… Actually, I wonder- are the targets' induced memories susceptible to being erased by the shooter effect? Could you get shot with it and lose the use of one arm, and then shoot someone else and erase your arm injury, and find that the loss of function is gone? What would that subjective experience be like?)

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
First, why would it be meaningless? Anything that has varying degrees can be measured, you just need to come up with a base unit. Obviously being called an idiot inflicts a very minor amount of psychological trauma, while being berated at great length and detail about your failings in front of your peers inflicts a great deal more. With a large enough sample size, a reasonable aproximation of an objective scale could be developed.

Second, I read this line very differently. I interpreted it as meaning that the gun inflicts the psychological eqivalent of of that much physical trauma. Objective pain metrics are a real thing used by doctors specializing in pain management, so it's perfectly reasonable that MCD could have developed one for their own uses.
